Borrow Fire, Then Become Fire · 02 / 05

Understanding: finite inquiry in a changing world

The world keeps changing, while people and models understand it with limited attention, time, and accessible information. How can understanding guide action while remaining open to correction? This group first distinguishes world, process, model, and expression, then examines how memory and records carry the past into the present, allowing continuity and revision together.

Reasoning develops from relations that may not yet have clear wording: form a question, propose explanations, and compare checkable consequences. Preferences help select worthwhile directions; evidence and rules determine what supports a conclusion. Restrained abstraction then asks which relationships the current question requires. Computational guarantees, explanatory adequacy, and practical feasibility each call for their own grounds.

Essays in this stage

01

World, process, and expression

Distinguish world, process, model, and expression so representations guide action and meet correction.

02

The stream and time

Examine different rhythms of change, memory, and experience, preserving continuity and room for revision.

03

Reasoning within an unfinished stream

Form questions and candidate explanations from the event stream, develop checkable consequences, then ask about view selection and support for conclusions.

04

A preference harness: rules and preferences working together

Distinguish views selected by preference from support supplied by evidence and rules, clarifying which answers finite inquiry needs to preserve.

05

Finite inquiry and economical abstraction

Carry questions of views and support into sufficient representation and computation under finite conditions, distinguishing formal guarantees from worldly explanation.
